good.name: Room rent: Single Standard A/C room (eligible category)
good.quote: A. Room (Single Standard A/C room), Boarding and Nursing Expenses
good.explanation: Default room eligibility is Single Standard A/C room. This is industry-standard (not ‘any room’).

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months (for Section 2 & Section 4)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage (good as per your rules; not a red flag).

good.name: Specific illness waiting period: 24 months (for Section 2 & Section 4)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.
good.explanation: A 24-month specific disease/procedure waiting period is standard in the market.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (standard)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: 30-day initial waiting is standard for most health insurance policies.

bad.name: Restore benefit: only for unrelated illness (not same illness) and only once; not available for Section 1
bad.quote: There shall be automatic restoration of the Basic Sum Insured by 100% immediately upon exhaustion of the basic sum insured, once during the policy period. It is made clear that such restored Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness /disease/treatment unrelated to the illness /diseases/treatment for which claim/s was/were made.
bad.explanation: Restore is NOT usable for the same illness, and is limited to once. Also, it is stated as applicable only for Section 2 (so diabetes complications under Section 1 may not get restore). Under your mandatory reporting, this is worse than ‘restore for same illness’, so flagged as a downside.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (mandatory feature not stated as covered)
bad.quote: Associated medical expenses... do not include Cost of pharmacy and consumables, Cost of implants and medical devices and Cost of diagnostics.
bad.explanation: The wording does not state that consumables are covered as a benefit; and it explicitly excludes consumables from ‘associated medical expenses’ used for proportionate calculations. Since explicit consumables cover is not found, treat as not covered per your rule (gloves, syringes, PPE etc. can become out-of-pocket).

bad.name: Pre-hospitalization: only 30 days (not >60 days)
bad.quote: Relevant Pre Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 30 days prior to the date of Hospitalisation
bad.explanation: Pre-hospitalization coverage is limited to 30 days, which is at the lower end (not a strong feature).

bad.name: Post-hospitalization: only 60 days and also capped (7% up to ₹5,000 per hospitalization)
bad.quote: Post Hospitalization expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge... shall not exceed the sum equivalent to 7% of the hospitalization expenses subject to a maximum of Rs.5,000/- per hospitalization
bad.explanation: Post-hospitalization is only 60 days (minimum acceptable) and additionally capped at 7% with a ₹5,000 limit, which can be inadequate for follow-up medicines/tests.

bad.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus: not found (mandatory feature assumed absent)
bad.quote: Where the policy is issued for more than 1 year, the Basic Sum Insured including sublimits, cumulative bonus (if applicable), automatic restoration benefit (if applicable) is for each of the year
bad.explanation: The document does not specify any No Claim Bonus/renewal bonus accrual. As per your rule, if not found, assume it is not covered: Sum Insured may not grow on renewal.
